speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To better understand your chronic left shoulder pain without trauma, can you describe how the pain started and what activities make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. Given your diabetes and the nature of the pain, could you tell me if you notice any significant loss of range of motion, particularly difficulty lifting your arm forward or behind your back? Also, does the pain improve with rest or specific positions?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis) with potential concurrent diabetic arthropathy. The insidious onset, severe restriction in both active and passive range of motion, and significant night pain in a diabetic patient without trauma are classic presentations. I recommend requesting a Shoulder_Xray to rule out calcific tendinitis and an MRI to assess the extent of capsular thickening.
